description: WHERE A REGULATION LIVES, so this site can notice when it moves. v0.22.0 made a compliance rule a record; v0.37.0 let a model draft one from regulation text and a person approve it. Both of those are about the moment a rule is written, and neither of them has anything to say six months later when the agency renumbers a section or raises a threshold. This doctype is the pointer that was missing: a URL, the regime it serves, how often to look, and a hash of what was there last time. IT DETECTS AND IT DOES NOT REMEDIATE, and that line is the whole design rather than a limitation of this release. A changed page is evidence that somebody should read the regulation again — not evidence about what it now says, and certainly not authority to rewrite a rule that is firing on somebody's compliance calendar. So a detected change writes a timestamp, a hash and a log entry naming the rules that were derived from this source, and stops. What happens next is a person reading the diff and, if a rule genuinely needs to change, `propose_compliance_rule` drafting the replacement and `approve_compliance_rule` putting a name on it. THE HASH IS OF NORMALISED TEXT rather than of the bytes, because a page carrying its own 'last updated 14:02' would otherwise report a change every single time it was checked, and an alarm that is always on is an alarm nobody reads. See `erpnext_mcp/services/regulation_feed.py` for exactly what is normalised away and what is deliberately kept.

fields.description: The docname, and what somebody scanning the register reads. Name it after the regulation rather than after the website: 'OAR 437-004 Agricultural Labor' is a source anybody on the operation can place, and 'OSHA page' is a row nobody can tell from the other three.
fields.label: Feed

fields.description: The http(s) URL that is checked. Point it at the NARROWEST page that carries the rule — a division of the rulebook rather than the rulebook's index, a specific Federal Register document rather than the search results that found it. A broad page changes for reasons that have nothing to do with this operation, and every one of those is a person asked to read a regulation for nothing.
fields.label: URL

fields.description: The audit this source answers to: OR-OSHA, FSMA, WPS, GAP, GlobalGAP, PrimusGFS, NOP, OTCO, Internal. It is how somebody preparing for one inspection finds the sources that bear on it, and how list_regulation_changes narrows 'what moved' to the scheme somebody is actually working on.
fields.label: Regime

fields.description: The entity this source is watched on behalf of. A multi-entity operation whose entities hold different certificates watches different sources, and the scoping is what keeps one entity's compliance officer out of the other's register.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: How often the sweep looks. THE CRON RUNS DAILY WHATEVER THIS SAYS — a Frappe cron expression is a static string in hooks.py and cannot be rewritten from a form — so this is a floor rather than a clock: Weekly means the sweep skips this feed until its last check is seven days old. Daily is for a source in an active rulemaking; Monthly is right for a certifier's handbook, which changes when the certifier says so and not on a schedule.
fields.label: Check Frequency

fields.description: PAUSED IS THE KILL SWITCH AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE PER FEED. A paused feed is skipped by the sweep and by check_all_regulation_feeds, and stays skipped until a person unpauses it — which is the right control for a source that has moved, gone behind a login, or started answering with a page that changes every time it is fetched. ERROR IS NOT A KILL SWITCH: it is what the last check reported, the sweep retries an errored feed on its next turn, and a successful check clears it back to Active. A source that was unreachable for an afternoon must not be a source nobody checks again.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: What is at that URL, in the words of somebody who has read it: which subject, which sections, and what on this operation turns on it. It is what a person reads when the change log says this source moved, and it is the difference between 'go and read a rulebook' and 'go and check whether the shade requirement changed'.
fields.label: Description

fields.description: The Compliance Rules that were written from this source. INFORMATIONAL, in one direction only: a change detected here names these rules in the log so a reader knows where to look, and nothing in this app edits, disables or supersedes a rule because a page changed. Updating a rule is still propose_compliance_rule drafting it and approve_compliance_rule putting a name on it.
fields.label: Rules Derived From This Source

fields.description: When this source was last successfully asked. Written by the sweep and by check_regulation_feed; empty means it has never been checked, which is why the first check is a BASELINE rather than a change.
fields.label: Last Checked

fields.description: When the normalised content last differed from the hash recorded before it. THIS IS THE FIELD list_regulation_changes SORTS AND FILTERS ON — 'what regulations moved since our last compliance review' is that query and nothing more.
fields.label: Last Change Detected

fields.description: SHA-256 of the NORMALISED content at the last successful check — tags, scripts, comments, timestamps, dates and clock times taken out, whitespace collapsed. Not of the bytes: a page that stamps itself with the minute it was served would otherwise report a change on every check, and a detector that always fires detects nothing. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a change that is ONLY a date — a compliance deadline moved from March 1 to April 1 — is invisible to this hash, and the note in services/regulation_feed.py says what to do about it.
fields.label: Last Content Hash

fields.description: What the last check failed with, when it failed. Cleared by the next check that succeeds, so a message here is about now rather than about something that was fixed in April.
fields.label: Last Error

fields.description: Every change, error and recovery this feed has seen, one timestamped line each, oldest first. APPEND-ONLY: no entry is ever edited, and when the log reaches its cap the OLDEST lines are dropped with a line saying so rather than the newest being refused — a log that stopped recording would be a detector that had quietly switched itself off. A CHANGED line carries the hash it moved from, the hash it moved to, the size of the normalised text, and the rule_ids of every rule derived from this source, because the sentence a reader needs is 'this moved and these three rules were written from it'.
fields.label: Change Log

name: Regulation Feed
